description: We welcome collaboration with innovative minds, creative thinkers, and passionate problem-solvers. We value diverse perspectives, technical expertise, and a shared vision for building impactful solutions.
summary: Most satellite applications recklessly blend data from both MODIS and VIIRS, causing an artificial 2472% rise in 2012. Continuum is an open source planetary dashboard that addresses this problem. We built a statistics engine to accurately compute the “Bridge Ratio” of sensors, thus combining 26 years of NASA data with a 90% confidence interval. We built a 30-Day Predictive Risk Calendar by blending the historic patterns with current wind forecast from Open-Meteo. For protection of citizens, we created a Community Hub and a Discord Bot. Citizens can report fires through chat or website and our backend verifies the fires by our multi-factor verification engine – a 15Km satellite telemetry verification, real time weather conditions (hot and dry) and 3 votes of community. Deterministic Parsing as opposed to AI allows us to create a 100% reliable alerting system with zero latency.
details:
What it does and how it works:
Continuum corrects the "phantom trend" in historical fire data. During the transition from MODIS (1km) to VIIRS (375m), the newer sensors recorded smaller fires, causing an artificial spike in 2012. We compute the empirical scale factor (k) between sensors on overlapping days, correcting for 98% of that artifact. Using our harmonized dataset, we build a 30-day Predictive Risk Calendar by combining historical fire probability with 7-day forecasted wind data. Finally, our Community Hub and Discord Bot empower citizens to submit anomaly reports. A backend multi-factor engine verifies the report: 1) A 15km Haversine satellite check, 2) Real-time Open-Meteo weather thresholds (temperature, humidity, wind), and 3) A 3-vote community consensus system.

Benefits and Intended Impact:
Our work bridges the gap between raw NASA data and practical implementation. Scientists get a statistically valid 26-year record with uncertainty intervals. Officials can plan ahead using our predictive risk calendar. Citizens can report fires through the web dashboard or Discord server, which are instantly cross-checked. For critical emergency alerts, we chose a deterministic parsing engine over LLMs to guarantee zero latency and eliminate hallucination risks.

Tools, Coding Languages, and Software Used:

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, MapLibre GL, Three.js (3D globe with SGP4 orbital propagation).
  • Backend: Node.js, Express-style API, Discord.js.
  • APIs: Open-Meteo (Geocoding and Weather Forecast), NASA FIRMS, NASA POWER, NASA GIBS, CelesTrak, and Natural Earth.

Creativity and Factors Considered:
We took into account the physical nature of fire—weather and human observation play massive roles. We integrated a 3D orbiting observatory to visualize satellite trajectories, a wind simulator to show smoke direction, and an interactive "Laika" space dog. Our multi-factor verification engine doesn't just reject a report if a satellite misses it (due to clouds); it checks weather conditions and empowers the community to verify it. The backend is engineered to handle API rate limits and gracefully fall back to bundled data if the live NASA API goes down.

Developer API & Ecosystem:
Continuum is not a closed system. We provide a fully documented REST API. Developers can generate API keys to access our harmonized 26-year record, fetch 30-day predictive risk calendars (/outlook), and retrieve community reports (/community/feed). We also built a dedicated webhook endpoint (/community/discord-sync) that allows our Discord bot to seamlessly push field reports directly to the web dashboard.
